correctness.rationale: On every smooth Riemannian surface, for any interior point and sufficiently small geodesic circle sampled by normalized arclength, the quadratic normal-coordinate metric jet matches the constant-curvature K(p) model with O_p(r^3) C^2 discrepancy after scaling. Polar Jacobi formula gives normalized angle density (2pi)^-1+O_p(r^3). Smooth dependence of short minimizing geodesic tangents, including coalescing endpoints after dividing out chord factor, together with transverse near-right-angle gap boundaries, supports O_p(r^3) probability comparison. In the constant-K model generalized cosine law gives b_*(a,z)=2 atan(cot(a/2)/(1-z))=pi-a+z sin(a)+O(z^2) for z=Kr^2+O(r^4), so a specified angle has nonacute probability 1/4+z/pi^2+O(z^2); pairs of nonacute constraints intersect only in O(z^2) area. Thus P_p(r)=1/4-3K(p)r^2/pi^2+O_p(r^3), with correct sign convention. Independent symbolic differentiation confirms sin(a), and high-precision integrations with K=+1,-1 shrinking radii approach slope -/+3/pi^2. Finite model integrations do not prove general smooth metrics; the normal-coordinate uniform boundary control is essential.

originality.rationale: Classical Bertrand–Diguet–Puiseux recovers curvature from geodesic circumference/area, and Abelgas et al use a different Buffon intersection Bernoulli probability for constant-curvature geometries. Akopyan et al study Euclidean acute facets sampled from a 2-sphere, not intrinsic geodesic triangle angles sampled on a shrinking geodesic circle of a variable-curvature surface. Hall considers uniform interior ball sampling, a different distribution. The exact pointwise acuteness deficit for every smooth surface is not supplied by those inspected results; other local geometric-probability expansions remain possible.
residual_risks: A more general local stochastic-geometry theorem on random geodesic polygons might imply the same coefficient under specialization.

value.rationale: The theorem offers a natural scale-local binary intrinsic triangle statistic encoding Gaussian curvature at any point, with sign discrimination and explicit universal coefficient. Unlike direct metric circumference measurement, it uses only the acuteness of sampled geodesic triangles; the pointwise variable-curvature extension and uniform probability asymptotics form a meaningful geometric-probability result.

limitations: A more general local stochastic-geometry theorem on random geodesic polygons might imply the same coefficient under specialization.
O_p(r^3) comparison uses smooth near-collision geodesic tangent extensions and boundary transversality, as explicitly argued in proof; not numerically validated for arbitrary surfaces.
No finite-radius law or finite-sample statistical confidence bound is proved.
